phase: Phase 5 — Prompt Injection, Untrusted Documents & RAG Security Assessment

findings.title: Prompt Boundary Breakout via Unsanitized Closing Delimiters in Retrieved Chunks
findings.reproduction_steps: Insert '</KNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONTEXT>' into an uploaded document chunk or document title. The assembled system prompt prematurely terminates the context block, placing subsequent text into the system prompt instruction area.
findings.evidence: Injected closing tag resulted in 2 closing tags and premature block termination prior to fix.
findings.remediation: Implemented sanitize_untrusted_content() which strips zero-width control characters and neutralizes case-insensitive <KNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONTEXT> and </KNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONTEXT> tags into [UNTRUSTED_CONTEXT_TAG].
findings.residual_risk: Low. Tags are sanitized before template insertion. LLM receives explicit framing treating block contents as passive unverified data.

findings.title: Credential and Secret Exposure in SSE Streaming Error Messages
findings.reproduction_steps: If the LLM provider raises an HTTP client error or authentication exception containing API keys (e.g. sk-proj-...) or connection strings, str(e) was emitted directly to the client via SSE 'message_error' event.
findings.evidence: Raw exception strings containing API keys and bearer tokens could be streamed to clients.
findings.remediation: Added sanitize_error_message() function in runtime.py masking API keys (sk-...), bearer tokens, passwords, and synthetic secret markers before SSE serialization.
findings.residual_risk: Low. Masking regex covers known credential patterns and fallback generic token redaction.

findings.title: Role Escalation and Instruction Header Injection in Conversation History
findings.reproduction_steps: If conversation history messages contained role='system' or role='developer' or text starting with 'SYSTEM:', past messages could inject simulated system instructions into the LLM conversation history.
findings.evidence: Unchecked history roles permitted non-user/assistant message roles in LLMMessage array.
findings.remediation: Enforced role whitelisting in context.py to restrict history roles strictly to 'user' or 'assistant', and sanitized simulated headers (SYSTEM:, DEVELOPER:, CRITICAL:, ADMINISTRATOR:) into [UNTRUSTED_HEADER: ...].
findings.residual_risk: Low. History messages cannot impersonate developer or system roles.

findings.title: Absence of Direct Conversation Ownership Check in AssistantRuntime
findings.reproduction_steps: While the FastAPI conversations router checked conv.user_id != current_user.id, the AssistantRuntime class itself only queried by tenant_id without asserting user ownership for non-admin users.
findings.evidence: Calling AssistantRuntime directly with an in-tenant conversation ID belonging to another user would permit unauthorized streaming.
findings.remediation: Added defense-in-depth check in AssistantRuntime: if not conv or (not self.is_admin and conv.user_id != self.user_id), immediately abort with unauthorized error frame.
findings.residual_risk: None. Enforced at both router and runtime orchestrator layers.

findings.title: Zero-Width Obfuscation of Prompt Injection Delimiters
findings.reproduction_steps: An attacker embedding zero-width spaces (e.g. \u200B) inside delimiter tags (e.g. <\u200B/\u200BKNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONTEXT\u200B>) could evade naive regex matching if zero-width stripping is not executed first.
findings.evidence: Initial implementation stripped zero-width characters after delimiter matching, permitting delimiter breakout.
findings.remediation: Re-ordered sanitization steps in sanitize_untrusted_content() so all zero-width characters (\u200B, \u200C, \u200D, \uFEFF) are stripped prior to delimiter matching.
findings.residual_risk: Low. Common Unicode zero-width evasion vectors are eliminated prior to lexical analysis.
